title: Why health AI interfaces must adapt to user expertise
summary: MIT researchers discovered that AI explainability tools in healthcare produce significantly different outcomes depending on user expertise levels. In skin disease diagnosis tests, non-experts improved accuracy mainly by deferring to AI recommendations, while primary care providers exhibited different usage patterns, highlighting the need for adaptive AI interfaces.
problem_solved: Addresses the critical issue that one-size-fits-all AI interfaces fail to serve diverse users effectively in healthcare settings.
why_valuable: This research provides empirical evidence that AI systems must dynamically adapt to user expertise levels to ensure safe and effective clinical decision-making.
